cl|us-tx: Chile and Texas both have a white star on blue with white and red horizontal stripes. Texas's blue runs the full height of the hoist as a vertical band; Chile's blue is only a square in the upper corner.
fr|us-ia: France and Iowa both have vertical blue, white and red stripes. France is plain; Iowa has a bald eagle, a streamer and the word IOWA on a wider white stripe.
gb|us-hi: The United Kingdom's Union Jack appears in Hawaii's canton. The UK flag is the Union Jack alone; Hawaii adds eight white, red and blue stripes.
lu|us-mo: Luxembourg and Missouri are both red, white and blue horizontal stripes. Luxembourg is plain with a light blue bottom stripe; Missouri has a coat of arms ringed by 24 stars in the center.
mk|us-nm: New Mexico and North Macedonia both show a sun in red and yellow. New Mexico has a red Zia sun with rays in four bundles on yellow; North Macedonia has a yellow sun with eight rays reaching the edges on red.
nl|us-mo: The Netherlands and Missouri are both red, white and blue horizontal stripes. The Netherlands is plain; Missouri has a coat of arms with two grizzly bears ringed by 24 stars.
us-al|us-fl: Alabama and Florida are both a red saltire on white. Alabama's is plain; Florida has the round state seal where the arms cross.
us-ct|us-vt: Connecticut and Vermont both show a single shield-like emblem on blue with a ribbon below. Connecticut's is a white shield with three grapevines; Vermont's is a landscape with a tall pine tree and a cow, topped by a deer's head.
us-de|us-nj: Delaware and New Jersey both use blue and buff. Delaware is blue with its arms in a buff diamond; New Jersey is a buff field with two women flanking a blue shield.
us-id|us-mt: Idaho and Montana are both a state seal on blue with the state's name. Idaho writes STATE OF IDAHO on a red banner below; Montana writes MONTANA in gold letters above.
us-il|us-ma: Illinois and Massachusetts are both a seal-style emblem on white. Illinois shows a bald eagle on a rock with ILLINOIS beneath; Massachusetts shows a blue shield with a Native American figure and no state name.
us-ks|us-mt: Kansas and Montana both put a seal and the state's name in gold on blue. Kansas has KANSAS below and a sunflower on top; Montana has MONTANA above the seal.
us-ks|us-ne: Kansas and Nebraska are both a state seal on dark blue. Kansas has a sunflower above the seal and KANSAS below; Nebraska's seal is plain gold and silver with no name underneath.
us-ky|us-va: Kentucky and Virginia are both commonwealths with a seal on dark blue. Virginia's seal is on a white disc and shows a woman standing over a fallen tyrant; Kentucky's shows two men shaking hands, ringed by its name and goldenrod.
us-ky|us-wi: Kentucky and Wisconsin both show two men in a seal on blue. Kentucky's men shake hands, with COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY above; Wisconsin's sailor and miner flank a shield, with WISCONSIN above and 1848 below.
us-me|us-mi: Maine and Michigan both have a moose in their arms on blue. In Maine the moose lies under a pine tree, with a farmer and sailor beside the shield; in Michigan an elk and a moose hold the shield, with a bald eagle on top.
us-me|us-nh: Maine and New Hampshire are both a central emblem on blue. New Hampshire's is a round seal of a ship on the stocks in a yellow wreath; Maine's is a shield held by a farmer and a seaman, with "MAINE" below.
us-me|us-vt: Maine and Vermont both have arms with a pine tree on blue. Maine's shield has a moose under the pine, held by a farmer and a sailor; Vermont's has a cow and wheat sheaves, with a deer's head on top.
us-mi|us-nd: Michigan and North Dakota both show an eagle on dark blue. North Dakota's eagle fills the flag on its own with a red "North Dakota" scroll; Michigan's eagle perches on top of a shield held by an elk and a moose.
us-mi|us-wi: Michigan and Wisconsin both show a coat of arms with supporters on blue. Michigan's supporters are an elk and a moose under a bald eagle; Wisconsin's are a sailor and a miner, with WISCONSIN written above.
us-mt|us-sd: Montana and South Dakota both write the state name in gold around a seal on blue. South Dakota's seal is ringed by a gold sunburst with "THE MOUNT RUSHMORE STATE" below; Montana's name sits in a straight line above.
us-mt|us-wi: Montana and Wisconsin are both blue with an emblem and the state name above it. Wisconsin's name is white with "1848" below and a badger on the shield; Montana's name is gold, with a round seal of mountains and waterfalls.
us-nc|us-tx: North Carolina and Texas both have a blue hoist band with a white star beside two horizontal stripes. Texas is white over red; North Carolina is red over white and adds the letters N and C and two dated scrolls.
us-ne|us-or: Nebraska and Oregon both show a monochrome gold emblem on blue. Oregon writes "STATE OF OREGON" and "1859" around its shield; Nebraska's round seal has no name outside it and shows a blacksmith and a train.
us-nh|us-vt: New Hampshire and Vermont are both a central emblem on blue. Vermont's is a shield with a pine tree and a cow under a stag's head; New Hampshire's is a round seal of a ship in a yellow wreath of stars.
us-nj|us-ny: New Jersey and New York both show a shield held by two standing women. New Jersey's field is buff with ploughs on the shield; New York's is dark blue with a sunrise over the Hudson.
us-ny|us-pa: New York and Pennsylvania both put a shield with an eagle on top on dark blue. New York's shield is held by two women; Pennsylvania's by two black horses.
us|us-hi: The United States and Hawaii both have horizontal stripes and a canton. The US has red and white stripes with 50 stars on blue; Hawaii has white, red and blue stripes with the Union Jack.
us|us-oh: The United States and Ohio both use red and white stripes with white stars on blue. Ohio's flag is a swallowtail with the stars in a blue triangle round a red-and-white circle; the US flag is a rectangle with a blue canton.
